;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Maghreb insurgency]]
**At least 10 [[Armed Forces of the Republic of Ivory Coast|Ivorian soldiers]] are killed and six others wounded at the [[Burkina Faso–Ivory Coast border|border]] with [[Burkina Faso]] when an armed group ambushed them; one of the attackers was also killed. It is the first attack in the country since the [[2016 Grand-Bassam shootings]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/10-soldiers-killed-attack-ivory-coast-border-post-200611143031833.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Disasters and accidents
*The death toll from the [[list of migrant vessel incidents on the Mediterranean Sea|sinking]] of a ship carrying 53 migrants off the coast of [[Tunisia]] on Tuesday rises to at least 46 as more bodies are recovered from [[Mediterranean Sea|the sea]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tunisia-migrants/death-toll-in-migrant-ship-disaster-off-tunisia-rises-to-46-idUSKBN23I1OT (Reuters)]
*The [[Ministry of Emergency Management]] of [[Government of China|China]] says that flooding in south and central [[China]] has killed more than a dozen people and forced hundreds of thousands to seek emergency shelter since 2 June. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/flooding-forces-hundreds-thousands-homes-china-200611060707197.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The [[United States]] surpasses two million cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], the first country in the world to do so. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/11/health/us-coronavirus-thursday/index.html (CNN)]

;International relations
*[[Iraq–United States relations]], [[Withdrawal of U.S. troops from Iraq (2020)]]
**The [[United States]] and [[Iraq]] begin negotiations, conducted remotely, to discuss the [[Withdrawal of U.S. troops from Iraq (2020)|withdrawal of U.S. troops]] and countering [[Iran]]ian influence. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/10/world/middleeast/iraq-isis-strategic-dialogue-troops.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[United States war crimes]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] authorizes sanctions against the [[International Criminal Court]] in retaliation for their investigation into potential [[war crime]]s by U.S. officials. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/06/11/politics/icc-executive-order/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*[[Bærum mosque shooting]]
**A court in [[Norway]] sentences Philip Manshaus to 21 years in prison for the racially-motivated murder of his stepsister and for attempting to kill [[Islam in Norway|Muslim]] worshippers. It is the longest prison sentence allowed by [[Law of Norway|law]]. The prison term contains a provision that his release can be put off indefinitely should he still be considered a threat to society. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/norway-sentences-oslo-mosque-shooter-21-years-prison-200611083805762.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Turkey–United States relations]], [[2016–present purges in Turkey]]
**A court in [[Turkey]] sentences a [[Consulate General of the United States, Istanbul|U.S. Consulate]] employee, Metin Topuz, to 8 years and 9 months in prison on charges of aiding the followers of [[Fethullah Gülen]], the U.S.-based preacher who is accused in Turkey of being the mastermind behind a [[2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt|failed coup attempt in 2016]] against [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan|Erdoğan]]. The U.S. Embassy in [[Ankara]] releases a statement on Twitter saying officials were "deeply disappointed" in the decision. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/11/world/europe/turkey-court-sentences-metin-topuz.html (''The New York Times'')]
*An attacker, believed to be a former student, kills the [[deputy head teacher|deputy head]] and injures five others with a knife at a school in [[Vrútky]], [[Slovakia]], before being killed by responding police officers. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53006785 (BBC News)]
*The [[Senate of Colombia|Senate of the Republic of Colombia]] approves a resolution banning the [[Testing cosmetics on animals|testing of cosmetics on animals]], as well as the commercialization of cosmetics which are actively tested on animals. [https://www.lafm.com.co/politica/colombia-ya-no-tendra-pruebas-de-cosmeticos-en-animales (La FM)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Dalton Tagelagi]] is elected new [[Premier of Niue]] by the [[Niue Assembly|Assembly]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/418748/dalton-tagelagi-voted-in-as-new-premier-of-niue (RNZ)]

;Sports
*[[2020 AFL season]], [[George Floyd protests in Australia]]
**After a ten-week suspension due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia|COVID-19 pandemic]], the 2020 AFL season resumes with [[Collingwood Football Club|Collingwood]] facing [[Richmond Football Club|Richmond]] at the [[Melbourne Cricket Ground|MCG]]. Before the match began, both teams knelt to show solidarity with the [[George Floyd protests]]. The match finished in a draw. [https://www.news.com.au/sport/afl-2020-collingwood-vs-richmond-live-scores-news-updates-from-mcg/live-coverage/df997ed6b22e812d91771b39582e4b71 (News.com.au)]
